- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.4), model often overshoots upward; cap forecast gains or reduce slope to prevent overbought momentum.  
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20-25 days horizon); add a small upward bias for final 5-7 days if sentiment remains positive.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion; if sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast to reflect gradual recovery.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates true price volatility in the final 10-15 days; apply a small upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
